key_insight: An automated AI pipeline can curate CMR reports and train multimodal vision models to diagnose major cardiomyopathies and cardiac amyloidosis with strong accuracy.
clinical_relevance: This could support faster, more standardized CMR interpretation and help scale expert-level cardiac disease detection in routine imaging workflows.
method: Used open-source locally run LLMs to extract diagnostic labels from narrative CMR reports.
Preprocessed cine and late-gadolinium-enhancement CMR sequences for multimodal model training.
Fine-tuned three vision foundation models (DINO, VST, UMedPT) and combined them with ensemble strategies.
evidence_signal: The study trained on 988 curated cases and evaluated performance on an independent test set of 1067 patients, with top AUCs reaching 0.966 for cardiac amyloidosis and 0.959 for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
watch_item: Performance is promising, but real-world deployment will need external validation across scanners, sites, and reporting styles before clinical use.
paper_title: Development of an automated, reliable, and clinically meaningful artificial intelligence (AI) tool for diagnosing cardiac disease from conventional cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) images
